reconcile.connective: Defenders read "seventy" as a round figure that excludes the concubine's son Abimelech and overlooks the one who escaped, so no real count is missing.

discrepancy.empty_note: The numerical tension (70 named in 8:30 versus the 71-72 implied once Abimelech and the surviving Jotham are added) is real, but no specific named historical critic could be verified as having pressed THIS Gideon-numbers passage in a citable work; the skeptic tradition that lists it (e.g. the Skeptic's Annotated Bible) is anonymous. Per guardrail 4, the discrepancy pole is left empty with relabel_flag rather than co-opting a fabricated critic.
discrepancy.relabel_reason: consensus is only probable_contradiction (not genuine), the gathered commentators (JFB, Gill) treat it as a soluble round-number / separate-mother convention, and no real named skeptic who engaged this specific passage could be verified. Route to a human to decide whether 'probable_contradiction' overstates a row that may be better labeled a soluble number convention.

excerpts.excerpt_text: threescore and ten persons—A round number is used, but it is evident that two are wanting to complete that number.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly addresses the numerical tension: JFB concedes the literal count falls short of seventy ('two are wanting') and explains 'threescore and ten' as a round number, which is the core harmonization of the 70-vs-71/72 discrepancy.

pd_work.resource: Jamieson, Fausset & Brown, Commentary Critical and Explanatory on the Whole Bible (1871), on Judges 9:5
pd_work.author: Jamieson, Fausset & Brown
pd_work.note: JFB treat this passage directly, explaining 'threescore and ten' as a round number and noting that two are wanting to complete it. Used as the PD anchor because Haley's specific coverage of this Gideon-numbers passage could not be confirmed and JFB is a harmonizing commentator already surfaced on this row keyed to the exact verse.
